cases.name: George Santos Announces New Run for Congress During State of the Union

sentences.1: In typically dramatic fashion, Santos announced his run while President Joe Biden delivered his State of the Union speech.
sentences.2: Three months after former Rep. George Santos' colleagues expelled him for a staggering array of alleged crimes and ethical violations, he has apparently decided that man cannot live by Cameo aloneâ€”and he wants his job back.
sentences.3: At least, Santos is officially running for Congress again, allowing him to raise money from the public and, potentially, spend it on his legal defense.
sentences.4: Santosâ€”an admitted liar who is currently indicted on 23 federal counts, including unemployment fraud, wire fraud, money laundering, stealing from his own campaign donors, and lying to Congressâ€”timed his announcement for maximum disruption: In the middle of President Joe Biden's State of the Union address.
sentences.5: Santos' announcement was, remarkably, not without precedent. The other two members who have been expelled since the Civil Warâ€”both Democratsâ€”went on to serve prison terms. Former Rep. James Trafficant, however, ran for Congress from his cell as an independent, losing to his former aide, Rep. Tim Ryan.
sentences.6: In fact, Santos wouldn't even be tied for this ignominious record, because Trafficant made another stab at his old seat in 2010, losing again to Ryan. The other expelled member, former Rep. Michael 'Ozzie' Myers, recidivated, pleading guilty in 2022 to election fraud for stuffing ballots for Democrats in Pennsylvania between 2014 and 2018. He's currently serving out the tail end of a 30-month prison sentence.
sentences.7: Still, the announcement caught many of Santos' former colleagues by surpriseâ€”though it was in keeping with his well-established pattern of false statements: He had previously claimed that he would not be running for re-election in his New York House seat.
sentences.8: "I will continue on my mission to serve my constituents up until I am allowed," Santos said in a social media statement following the release of the Ethics Committee report last November. "I will however NOT be seeking re-election for a second term in 2024 as my family deserves better than to be under the gun from the press all the time."
sentences.9: His official paperwork, filed with the Federal Election Commission on Thursday nightâ€”minutes after a wave of "scam PACs" submitted expense reportsâ€”shows that the impudent fraudster is also switching districts, going from New York's 3rd to New York's 1st. He opened a new campaign committeeâ€”simply called "Santos for Congress"â€”rather than repurposing his old campaign, "Devolder-Santos for Congress," which is still carrying unpaid debts.
sentences.10: The move to New York's 1st District will pit him against incumbent GOP Rep. Nick LaLotaâ€”one of Santos' chief antagonists, who in October filed a motion to expel him.
sentences.11: Santos was, of course, eventually dismissed, following the release of a House Ethics Committee report in November detailing a wide range of alleged criminal and unethical behavior. His old seat is now held by Democratic Rep. Tom Suozzi, who won a special election last month.
sentences.12: For his part, Santos has since embraced a side gig selling personalized videos, generating potentially his first genuine six-figure income in a matter of weeks.
sentences.13: But on Thursday night, Santos took advantage of his former member privileges to attend the State of the Union. Sporting a silver-spangled dress collar and shoes to match, he spent much of his time on the floor ahead of the speech attempting to yuk it up with his former colleagues.
sentences.14: Santos could be seen chatting with fellow embattled Rep. Matt Gaetz (R-FL), as well as Reps. Lauren Boebert (R-CO) and Tim Burchett (R-TN). He even appeared to pose for a selfie with Rep. Matt Rosendale (R-MT).
sentences.15: "Clownshow," one GOP member said of Santos being at the State of the Union. "Him keeping his privileges was an oversight that may soon be corrected."
sentences.16: Santos posted a social media statement shortly after his official paperwork was submitted, claiming that he has "made several personal sacrifices in the name of serving the American people" lifting a phrase from defeated GOP presidential candidate Ron DeSantis.
sentences.17: "My promise is that I will never back down because of my love for this country," Santos wrote, claiming that he "left office arbitrarily" due to pressure from his former GOP colleagues in New Yorkâ€”chiefly targeting his primary opponent, LaLota.
sentences.18: Santos said he came to his decision following "a lot of prayer and conversation with my friends and family," and hopes the move "will shake things up."
sentences.19: One of Santos' former New York colleagues, Rep. Marc Molinaro (R-NY)â€”who helped lead the effort to oust Santosâ€”laughed when asked what he thought of the disgraced former congressman's appearance at the vaunted address.
sentences.20: Then, upon first learning of the news, five New York Republicansâ€”Reps. Nick Langworthy, Nick LaLota, Anthony DeEsposito, Mike Lawler, and Molinaroâ€”audibly laughed while the State of the Union was going on. When another GOP member was told Santos was running, they offered a short response: "From jail?"
sentences.21: Santos' criminal trial is scheduled for September, meaning that, should he pull off a miracle in the primary, Santos, like Donald Trump, may face the daunting task of convincing voters to cast their ballot for a convicted, and potentially prison-bound, felon.
sentences.22: Santos has pleaded not guilty to the charges, denies wrongdoing, and has emitted only narrow expressions of remorse.
sentences.23: But Santosâ€”who lied repeatedly to his previous constituents, including about basic biographical factsâ€”faces an uphill battle there, though his candidacy might be about something else entirely.
sentences.24: If Santos is indeed modeling his bid after Trump, he could theoretically raise money from the public and use it to help offset his legal bills. Of course, his old campaign committee must also pay down its still outstanding legal debt of roughly $70,000, along with obligations to former campaign staffers, an Italian restaurant with sketchy family ties, and a direct mail company currently at the center of a separate congressional ethics scandal involving Rep. Alex Mooney (R-WV).
sentences.25: His old campaign's year-end report, filed at the end of January, showed roughly $11,400 in donations. A number of contributions rolled in after his expulsion, including from a donor group that The Daily Beast previously tied to the indicted Chinese right-wing financier Guo Wengui.
sentences.26: Regardless of how long Santos' campaign lasts, his fundraising and spending will draw some of the heaviest scrutiny in the country. His candidacy statement shows that this unenviable job will fall to his most recent treasurer, whose work for Santos was never flagged by federal regulators.
sentences.27: Santos' former campaign treasurer, Nancy Marks, entered into a cooperation agreement with federal prosecutors last October, pleading guilty to collaborating with her former client to file false FEC reports in an attempt to inflate his fundraising and cover up fake donations. Last week, Marks asked the court to delay her sentencing until Novemberâ€”after the Santos trial, and after the general election.

Explanation.explanation: Attacking the person's character (liar, fraudster) instead of addressing the argument about his congressional run.
Assuming the behavior of past expelled members predicts Santos' future actions, without addressing his current intentions.
Assuming that Santos facing a trial and potentially being prison-bound will lead to difficulties convincing voters to support him based on a comparison to Donald Trump's situation.
Drawing conclusions about Santos' fundraising and spending based on potential comparisons to Donald Trump without sufficient evidence or logical connection.

cases.name: Disaster for Trump as Truth Social Crashes at Critical SOTU Moment

sentences.1: Donald Trump may have rage-posted his way through President Joe Biden's State of the Union address on Truth Social, but his social media site crashed for many before Biden even entered the House chamber, with technical issues lingering for at least an hour before and into his remarks.
sentences.2: Beginning shortly before 9 p.m. EST Thursday, outages numbered in the thousands, according to Downdetector. The outages peaked an hour later and then began to slowly resume back to normal, according to the monitor.
sentences.3: Around the same time, users on X reported not being able to access Trump's feed, with some—including former Trump White House Press Secretary Alyssa Farah Griffin—mocking him for it.
sentences.4: "Trump said he'd be live fact-checking Biden's SOTU but Truth Social appears to be down. Sad!" she wrote on X.
sentences.5: On Fox News, meanwhile, anchor Bret Baier—who had read out loud some of Trump's posts—invited him to just call in.
sentences.6: "If the former president wants to call in," Baier said, likely speaking directly to Trump through the screen, "we're happy to put him [on] instead of just reading Truth Social posts."
sentences.7: Those who were able to see what Trump had to say were likely not surprised, as his posts were largely negative reactions to people he saw on the broadcast.
sentences.8: "Thankfully, we don't have to be looking at RINO Mitt Romney much longer!" Trump wrote of the retiring Utah senator who has opposed Trump's 2024 candidacy.
sentences.9: Trump, who incited a mob of supporters that broke into the Capitol and House chamber on Jan. 6, 2021, then accused Biden of being "very disrespectful to our country" because his address in that same chamber didn't begin promptly at 9 p.m.
sentences.10: He also predictably took aim at Biden during his speech, insisting the president was "angry and crazy" and that "the words are not flowing smoothly out of his mouth!"

Explanation.explanation: In this sentence, Trump attacks Biden personally by accusing him of being disrespectful without addressing the content of Biden's speech. This diverts attention from the actual arguments presented.

In this sentence, it is assumed that all of Trump's posts were negative reactions based on the limited sample of posts seen by some viewers. This draws a conclusion about the entirety of Trump's posts without considering the full scope.

cases.name: Kosher Phones Used by Ultra-Orthodox Jews

sentences.1: As an elder millennial, I received my first cell phone during my senior year of high school.
sentences.2: Today, smartphone addiction is widely acknowledged, and most people I know are actively seeking to minimize screen time and shield their children from the highly addictive nature of technology.
sentences.3: Ultra-orthodox groups are relatively secluded and are characterized by their strict adherence to Jewish law, particularly those concentrated in Israel and America but also found in various countries such as Australia, Canada, and England.
sentences.4: "I am a native New Yorker, but I saw zero footage of September 11th," Frieda Vizel told The Daily Beast.
sentences.5: She's a 39-year-old woman who grew up as part of New York's ultra-orthodox Satmar community but chose to leave that way of life more than a decade ago.
sentences.6: "The footage was completely inaccessible to me [in my community]." She grew up in the Hasidic Jewish town of Kiryas Joel in upstate New York, where she had no access to screens or television.
sentences.7: The resistance to embrace smart technologies unfolded gradually.
sentences.8: During the early 2000s, with technological advancements, some within the ultra-orthodox community began to buy some of the earliest versions of smartphones like Blackberries.
sentences.9: "After I got married [in the early 2000s], I had a mobile phone. Everyone in the community bought one," she recalled.
sentences.10: The technology was rapidly gaining popularity and was eagerly adopted.
sentences.11: However, the rabbis soon realized that smartphones, with their swiftly advancing features and fast internet speed, would be challenging to control and could jeopardize the community's way of life.
sentences.12: To counter this risk, smartphones were prohibited, and a novel approach emerged: "kosher" phones.
sentences.13: Kosher phones, often endorsed by rabbis for community use, typically come in two varieties.
sentences.14: They can be extremely simple phones with minimal features, like basic calling and no internet, while others are smart devices retrofitted with filters that can be updated and installed by designated individuals within the ultra-orthodox community at the time of purchase.
sentences.15: These filters guarantee that no distractions or apps conflicting with the expectations of the ultra-orthodox lifestyle are allowed.
sentences.16: While pornographic websites are obviously blocked, other more innocuous websites like YouTube or apps like Spotify may also be limited due their perceived incompatibility.
sentences.17: "When I first heard about them, I started to think, 'Is this going to catch on? Are they going to get people to turn in their smartphones and get people to buy these basic phones?'" said Vizel.
sentences.18: A quick walk around any ultra-orthodox Jewish enclave anywhere in the world will show that the ban on smartphones has been remarkably successful.
sentences.19: "It is mind boggling to me to see the rate of success. In Hasidic Williamsburg, you see kosher phones everywhere and you rarely see a smartphone," Vizel said. "I watched this happen in real time, and I thought it was impossible."
sentences.20: In contrast to the ubiquitous online presence in today's hyper-connected world, the ultra-orthodox community follows a different approach.
sentences.21: Adults may have access to internet-enabled devices for work or study, albeit with limitations and filters and they are not online all the time.
sentences.22: Access is never granted to children under the age of 18.
sentences.23: "There is an acceptance that smartphones and the internet are necessary," Vizel said.
sentences.24: However, they "try not to bring it into their life," and don't subscribe to "hyper-addicting smartphone culture."
sentences.25: Interestingly, Vizel finds that she is often recognized and spotted by members of her former community, who have clearly been watching her videos on YouTube, perhaps with a filter like KosherTube, which ensures content that is viewable and appropriate for members of an ultra-orthodox Jewish community.
sentences.26: "I have a ton of viewers on my YouTube channel who are Hasidic," she said. "But many don't have smartphones."
sentences.27: Even though kosher phones are widely used in ultra-orthodox communities, it does not necessarily result in lower levels of addiction.
sentences.28: Technology can prove to be incredibly enticing even with the filters and limited features.
sentences.29: "People can call hotlines and listen to the news, and people are enamoured by that," Vizel said. "One of the ubiquitous sights in Williamsburg is that there are people glued to their phones. [...] Kosher phones are addictive but in a different way."
sentences.30: Imposing restrictions on internet access also has its drawbacks.
sentences.31: Leah Boulton is the founder and CEO of Pathways Melbourne, a group dedicated to supporting and empowering ultra-Orthodox Jews who are questioning their lifestyle, practices and beliefs.
sentences.32: She told The Daily Beast that there are multiple challenges created by the technology.
sentences.33: For one, the use of kosher phones can complicate the process of challenging their beliefs, as filters may block access to supportive websites and hinder the acquisition of essential information.
sentences.34: "Often when we start engaging with people, they have managed to access some form of internet," she said. "Last year, we had a young man with two sim cards. He had a kosher and non-kosher one. It was very hard to contact him."
sentences.35: Boulton doesn't criticize anyone who uses a kosher phone. It's their individual choice.
sentences.36: However, it does lead to a more limited worldview. "And this controls the risks that may lead to questioning."
sentences.38: While imposing restrictions on oneself and family members can provide a sense of manageability for mobile phone users, issues arise when there is a need for broader access to the world, making kosher phones a significant concern.
sentences.39: "If a child or adult is in an unsafe family environment, kosher phones allow little means to see that what they are experiencing is unacceptable," Boulton explained.
sentences.40: Despite some of the drawbacks, adopting a simpler lifestyle with a kosher phone still triggers a yearning for Vizel—especially when she sees ultra-orthodox children enjoying life without being tethered to an iPad or smartphone.
sentences.41: "The community's success in keeping kids off social media and off the internet is predicated on all of them being in the same situation," she said. "If your kid is bored there are other children [who are] bored and want to play with them. These children have something special. It's almost impossible to replicate."

Explanation.explanation: The use of tradition as a reason to continue a certain practice without considering its validity or relevance to the current situation.

The appeal to tradition is evident in the community's decision to continue using "kosher" phones due to their traditional way of life, without fully evaluating the impact or necessity of maintaining this practice.
Drawing a premature conclusion without sufficient evidence or reasoning.

cases.name: Monolingual Trump Slams Migrants Who 'Don't Speak Languages'

sentences.1: Monolingual former President Donald Trump lashed out Thursday at immigrants to the United States who, as he put it, 'don't speak languages.'
sentences.2: While speaking at the U.S.-Mexico border in Eagle Pass, Texasâ€”the same day that President Joe Biden visited the border in Brownsvilleâ€”Trump echoed his increasingly angry and pessimistic approach to describing immigration to the United States.
sentences.3: 'They're coming from jails, and they're coming from prisons, and they're coming from mental institutions, and they're coming from insane asylums, and they're terrorists. They're being let into our country, and it's horrible,' said Trump, who not that long ago declared that those same people are 'poisoning the blood of our country.'
sentences.4: Trump then claimed that no one has given him a satisfactory answer on the topic.
sentences.5: 'Nobody can explain to me how allowing millions of people from places unknown, from countries unknown, who don't speak languagesâ€”we have languages coming into our countryâ€”we have nobody that even speaks those languages. They're truly foreign languages. Nobody speaks them,' he said. 'And they're pouring into our country, and they're bringing with them tremendous problems, including medical problems, as you know.'
sentences.6: CNN, which aired a portion of Trump's comments, cut away for a fact-check minutes later by reporter Daniel Dale, an editorial strategy that is becoming more prevalent among major news networks.
sentences.7: 'I asked the Trump campaign: what is the evidence that unnamed foreign leaders are emptying out their institutions, their jails, sending people here as migrants? They couldn't come up with anything,' Dale told anchor Kaitlan Collins.
sentences.8: Dale also addressed Trump's dismissive comments about languages.
sentences.9: 'He told the story that he's told before, Kaitlan, about people arriving speaking languages that no one's ever heard. He said in a previous, recent speech [that] we didn't even have one translator who could understand this language,' Dale said. 'This, I've looked into this; it seems to be just conjured out of thin air. It's nonsense.'

Explanation.explanation: Trump's claim that nobody can explain the situation of immigrants not speaking languages lacks evidence and presents a questionable conclusion.
Dale's investigation reveals that Trump's statement about people speaking unknown languages lacks foundation and is a false cause fallacy.

cases.name: The Traitors' Ep. 10 Recap: The Queen Is Dethroned in Shocking Twist

sentences.1: The Faithfuls just might have a chance of winning this thing, but the one remaining Traitor in the mix has already proved to be awfully sneaky.
sentences.2: As the Peacock series rolls up to its finale next week, we're down to just one Traitorâ€”Below Deck star and returning Traitors player Kate Chastain. Despite her claim at the start of her foray into Traitor-dom that she's a bad liar, Kate proved this week that she can be a master of misdirection and deception.
sentences.3: As usual, the Traitors got to choose a murder victim after the elimination, and this time, they chose former Parliament member and Pilot Pete ally John Bercowâ€”whose long speeches at the roundtables tend to sway the votes.

Explanation.explanation: The text implies that Kate Chastain is a master of misdirection and deception despite claiming she's a bad liar at the start. This implies that just because she claimed something at the beginning, it must be true throughout, which is an Appeal to Tradition fallacy.

The text suggests that the Traitors chose John Bercow as a murder victim, implying that his long speeches swaying the votes led to his selection. This is a Questionable Conclusion as it assumes a direct causal link between his speeches and being chosen as the victim without sufficient evidence.

The text mentions the Traitors choosing John Bercow as a murder victim and implies a causal relationship between his speeches swaying votes and his selection. This is a False Cause fallacy, as it assumes that his speeches directly caused his selection as a murder victim, without establishing a valid causal connection.

cases.name: Testy Exchange Between Hunter Biden, Matt Gaetz Revealed in Deposition Transcript

sentences.1: Rep. Matt Gaetz (R-FL) and Hunter Biden had a tense exchange Wednesday during the latter's testimony before the House Oversight Committee, with the president's son taking issue with Gaetz's line of questioning.
sentences.2: In the closed-door session, Biden called the impeachment probe into his father a 'partisan political pursuit' being pushed by 'MAGA-motivated conspiracies,' according to a transcript released by the committee Thursday.
sentences.3: Gaetz, a frequent defender of former President Donald Trump, questioned Biden about serving on the board of Burisma, a Ukrainian energy company. Gaetz wanted to know if Biden, a recovering addict, was 'on drugs' while on the board.
sentences.4: Biden's lawyer, Abbe Lowell, first took issue with that.
sentences.5: "One of the things that I spoke to staff that you just asked about as to whether it's outside the bounds. If you want to spend the next part of the last hour you have asking about his drug use, go at it," Lowell said. "It's outside the scope. It certainly has no relevance to an impeachment inquiry nor does it have anything to do with oversight of ethics legislation that may address family members of presidents or vice presidents. So go at it, but it's outside the scope and you're wasting your time."
sentences.6: Gaetz then repeated his question to Biden: 'Were you on drugs when you were on the Burisma board?'
sentences.7: Biden replied: 'Mr. Gaetz, look me in the eye. You really think that's appropriate to ask me?'
sentences.8: After Gaetz said it 'absolutely' was, Biden shot back: 'Of all the people sitting around this table, do you think that's appropriate to ask me?'
sentences.9: Biden may have been alluding to a series of salacious allegations against the Florida firebrand, including a Daily Beast report earlier this month revealing that in 2021 a young woman told prosecutors working on a sex trafficking investigation that she had sex with Gaetz at a party which she was paid to attend and where drugs were present. When approached for comment at the time, a Gaetz spokesperson said: 'Rep. Gaetz does not know anything about the woman you're referencing.'
sentences.10: Last February, federal prosecutors decided to close that investigation into Gaetz without filing charges. Gaetz is still facing an ongoing House Ethics Committee inquiry into allegations of sex crimes and drug use, among other things.
sentences.11: Gaetz has maintained that the inquiry is retaliation for his role in last year's ouster of House Speaker Kevin McCarthy.
sentences.12: "The Ethics Committee is engaging in payback against me for ousting the person who singularly appointed every Republicanâ€”Kevin McCarthy," he told ABC News earlier this month.
sentences.13: After Biden asked Gaetz whether his question was 'appropriate,' Gaetz replied, 'Yeah. Are you going to answer it?'
sentences.14: After a little more back-and-forth, Biden responded at length.
sentences.15: "I will answer it this way: I have been absolutely transparent about my drug use. Again, I spoke to you all earlier this morning about that. I'm sorry; I'm an addict. I was an addict. I have been in recovery for over four and a half years now, Mr. Gaetz. I work really, really hard at it," he said.
sentences.16: "Let me answer. I work really hard at it, under an enormous amount of pressure. Was I an addict? Yes, I was an addict. What does that have to do with whether or not you're going to go forward with an impeachment of my father other than to simply try to embarrass me?"

Explanation.explanation: Gaetz's focus on Biden's drug use instead of addressing the substantive issue of Biden's involvement with Burisma is an ad hominem attack.
Gaetz's insistence on Biden answering the drug use question diverts attention from the main topic under discussion.

cases.name: Donald Trump's Cash Crunch Just Got Much, Much Worse

sentences.1: As Donald Trump's legal troubles consume more and more of his time, they're also consuming more of his donors' moneyâ€”and there's a huge hole in the bucket.
sentences.2: On Tuesday, Trump's 'Save America' leadership political action committee reported raising just $8,508 from donors in the entire month of January, while spending about $3.9 million, according to a new filing with the Federal Election Commission.

Explanation.explanation: Mistaking correlation for causation in assuming that Trump's legal troubles consuming his time directly lead to consuming more donors' money.
Drawing unwarranted conclusions based on limited information or data.
Sidetracking from the main financial issues by focusing on Trump's campaign spending details.

cases.name: Kari Lake Comes Up Empty-Handed When Pressed About Arizona Election Claims

sentences.1: When it comes to Kari Lake's debunked theory of widespread election fraud in her 2022 Arizona gubernatorial race, she's not even sure 'who exactly stole the election,' she admitted Monday.
sentences.2: During an interview on Arizona's KTAR News 92.3 FM, Lake's false claims were challenged by the station's legal analyst, Barry Markson.
sentences.3: My question is, as you've been saying for three years, or for two years: can you tell us who stole the election from you and how they did it, and if you can't or you don't want to, that's OK, but I want to make sure the question is there in front of you, Markson said.
sentences.4: A post-election lawsuit from Lake alleging election fraud was rejected in December 2022, with an Arizona court ruling that there was no 'clear and convincing evidence' the race outcome was affected by fraud. Lake's additional legal losses extended through late last year. But that hasn't seemed to deter her.
sentences.5: I don't know who exactly stole the election, Lake said, 'but there are a lot of people who are running elections poorly, and we've seen the result.'
sentences.6: A candidate for Senate in Arizona this year, Lake added: 'The elections are run poorly. They're run very poorly, and I don't know who exactly.'
sentences.7: At another point in the interview, Lake tried to explain critical comments she made in 2022 about former Arizona Sen. John McCain and his supporters. But McCain's daughter, Megan, hasn't bought that Lake's remarks were made in jest.
sentences.8: Guess she realized she can't become a Senator without us, McCain wrote on X Tuesday.

Explanation.explanation: Kari Lake draws unwarranted conclusions about election fraud without considering the lack of clear evidence supporting her claims.
McCain hastily generalizes that Lake cannot become a Senator without their support based on her previous remarks.

cases.name: Roger Stone Caught on Tape Discussing Trump's Plan to Challenge 2024 Election

sentences.1: Self-proclaimed 'dirty trickster' Roger Stone was secretly videotaped at Mar-a-Lago during a remarkably candid conversation.
sentences.2: Roger Stone, a longtime Republican operative who served as an adviser to Donald Trump, was secretly recorded at Mar-a-Lago spilling the beans on the former president's strategy to challenge the results of the 2024 election should he lose again.
sentences.3: The self-described 'dirty trickster' of right-wing politics unknowingly divulged the plan to liberal reporters Lauren Windsor and Ally Sammarco, who posed as Trump fans and covertly videotaped him at a 'Catholics Prayer for Trump' event on March 19. The recordings were first reported by Rolling Stone.
sentences.4: The remarkably candid conversation is just the latest released by Windsor and her left-leaning sting group, The Undercurrent, in recent weeksâ€”and comes on the heels of headline-grabbing tapes that captured both Supreme Court Justice Samuel Alito and his wife, Martha-Ann Alito, weighing in on a number of hot button culture war issues facing the court and the country.
sentences.5: Stone, who was a key figure in Trump's 'Stop the Steal' efforts following the 2020 election, characterized his plan to challenge election results in 2024 with three pillars: 'Lawyers, judges, technology.' He also bragged that the Trump campaign occupied strong 'offensive footing' this time around.
sentences.6: 'In some states, it'll be easier to stop. In other places it won't,' Stone told Sammarco. 'At least this time when they do it, you have a lawyer and a judge, his home phone number standing by so you can stop it,' apparently referring to the certification of 2024 results.
sentences.7: 'We made no preparations last time, none,' he added.
sentences.8: Stone also tacitly endorsed storming the Capitol building after Sammarco told him she was at the insurrection.
sentences.9: 'That may not be necessary,' Stone continued. 'There are technical, legal steps we have to take to try to have a more honest election.'
sentences.10: Stone noted during the conversation that the Trump campaign is attempting to change state voting laws and plans to immediately file a number of lawsuits seeking to change the results should the former president lose again, as Trump allies did in Michigan and several other states in 2020.
sentences.11: 'We should be suing in a half a dozen places,' Stone said of the Michigan lawsuit, adding that the RNC's war chest would be tapped to fund the various lawsuits.
sentences.12: The Trump campaign launched 62 lawsuits contesting the results of the election across the country in 2020. However, most were quickly dismissed or dropped due to a lack of standing or evidence, according to Bloomberg Law.
sentences.13: Stone told Windsor that the Trump campaign even has governors who are ready to contest this November's election resultsâ€”though he qualified, candidly, that there 'aren't many' willing to put their reputation on the line in service of the former president.

Explanation.explanation: Roger Stone is appealing to tradition by suggesting that contesting election results through lawsuits is a valid approach because Trump allies did so in several states in 2020. However, the fact that something was done in the past does not necessarily make it the best or only way to handle election disputes.

Roger Stone implies that governors contesting election results in November is a reasonable action by pointing out that there are some governors willing to do so. This appeal to tradition assumes that following this pattern is valid without considering other perspectives or options.

The statement highlights the Trump campaign's launch of 62 lawsuits to contest election results in 2020 but fails to mention the outcome or reasons for the dismissal of most of these lawsuits, which could provide a more balanced view of the effectiveness of such legal actions. This selective presentation of information influences the perception of the Trump campaign's legal strategies.

cases.name: Jimmy Kimmel Fires Back at 'Preposterous' George Santos Lawsuit

sentences.1: After returning from what he described as an 'eventful' holiday weekend, Jimmy Kimmel on Tuesday had one question at the top of his mind: 'Did anyone else get sued by George Santos this weekend?'
sentences.2: More than two months after Kimmel, using a bevy of pseudonyms, got George Santos to record all sorts of bizarre Cameo videos—which the late-night host then promptly shared with viewers—the disgraced former congressman is now suing Kimmel, ABC, and Disney (the network's parent company) over the prank.
sentences.3: "I am currently embroiled in the most preposterous lawsuit of all time," Kimmel shared. "George Santos—a man Republicans kicked out of congress for being a fraud—is suing me for fraud!" Which the host thinks is quite rude, frankly, "because we did a nice thing. We supported him by ordering his Cameo videos."
sentences.4: Among the "absolutely ridiculous messages" Kimmel sent to Santos via Cameo were congratulations—and well wishes—for "Gary Fortuna for winning the Clearwater Florida Beef Eating Contest" by eating a record-breaking six pounds of ground beef in less than 30 minutes and promptly being hospitalized, and further congrats for Brenda "on the successful cloning of her beloved schnauzer Adolf."
sentences.5: Santos' reaction to the unexpected publicity was to demand an additional $20,000 from Kimmel for sharing the videos, but Kimmel made it clear he wasn't about to roll over for the man sometimes known as George Devolder. And Kimmel's opinion on the matter—which has now escalated to a request for $750,000 plus damages—does not seem to have changed.
sentences.6: "He says we deceived him under the guise of fandom soliciting personalized videos, only to then broadcast these on national television," Kimmel explained. "And if there's one thing George Santos won't stand for, it's using a fake name under false pretenses."
sentences.7: "He says he thought these were real messages and he was duped," Kimmel added of his video requests, noting that the serial fabulist is "being represented by the prestigious law firm of Pot, Kettle, and Black."
sentences.8: "This is like being sued for paternity by Nick Cannon," Kimmel concluded.

Explanation.explanation: Kimmel dismisses Santos' lawsuit by focusing on the fact that Santos was previously kicked out of Congress for being a fraud. This appeal to tradition implies that because Santos has a history of fraudulent behavior, his current lawsuit is unwarranted.

Kimmel concludes the situation by comparing it to being sued for paternity by Nick Cannon. This comparison is unwarranted and questionable, as the severity and context of the two scenarios are vastly different.

cases.name: The Washington Post

cases.name: Climate Protesters at Stonehenge

sentences.1: Officials Livid With Climate Protesters Who Sprayed Stonehenge Orange
sentences.2: Two climate protesters were arrested Wednesday after using orange cornstarch to temporarily paint Stonehenge orange.
sentences.3: According to a press release from the coalition Just Stop Oil, which organized the action, the Stonehenge demonstration is one part of a broader effort to push the incoming U.K. government to commit to signing 'a legally binding treaty to phase out fossil fuels by 2030.'
sentences.4: Speaking on the podcast PoliticsJOE, Just Stop Oil spokesman James Skeet emphasized the group's belief that the orange cornstarch will wash off of the prehistoric monument in a couple of days. In contrast, he said, 'the damage that is being done to all of our communities by oil and gas executives and the politicians that they've bought is going to run on for many generations.'
sentences.5: During the appearance, Skeet challenged listeners with a question: 'What is it that's more shocking—is it a bit of cornstarch on a treasured monument, or is it the fact that governments have admitted to burning more oil, gas, and coal when we're just coming off the back of 12 straight months of record temperatures that are leading to fires, floods, crop failures worldwide?'
sentences.6: The damage from climate inaction, Skeet said, is 'going to lead to millions of people killed and displaced in the years to come.'
sentences.7: Still, authorities and online spectators are about as livid as one might expect.
sentences.8: Prime Minister Rishi Sunak called the action a 'disgraceful act of vandalism,' according to NBC News. Sunak echoed the sentiment on X, where he called Just Stop Oil 'a disgrace.'
sentences.9: Meanwhile, curators for English Heritage—which manages Stonehenge as a UNESCO World Heritage Site—are investigating the damage and called the decoration 'extremely upsetting.' The site remains open to the public.
sentences.10: X is replete with negative reactions as well. As one commenter put it, 'I'm kind of with you on your campaign. But this? This doesn't work. This doesn't get people on side. It does the opposite. It's vandalism.'
sentences.11: Speaking on PoliticsJOE, Skeet emphasized that the demonstration has successfully placed the climate crisis at the top of the world news cycle, where it would not have been before. As for whether or not actions like this endear people to Just Stop Oil itself, he suggested that the question might be beside the point.
sentences.12: "There's ample research on this that suggest that though people don't like Just Stop Oil, they tend to actually disassociate it from the issue itself," Skeet said. "So, generally, people will be going, 'Oh, I don't like these Just Stop Oil folks, but actually, the issue of the climate crisis is really important, and something needs to happen about it."
sentences.13: The protesters themselves are equally adamant that something must be done.
sentences.14: Niamh Lynch, a 21-year-old student from Oxford, said in Just Stop Oil's press release, 'It's time for us to think about what our civilization will leave behind—what is our legacy? ... Standing inert for generations works well for stones—not climate policy.'
sentences.15: Rajan Naidu, a 73-year-old from Birmingham, added, 'Either we end the fossil fuel era, or the fossil fuel era will end us.'
sentences.16: Naidu continued: 'Just as fifty years ago, when the world used international treaties to defuse the threats posed by nuclear weapons, today the world needs a Fossil Fuel Non-Proliferation Treaty to phase out fossil fuels and to support dependent economies, workers and communities to move away from oil, gas and coal.'

Explanation.explanation: The statements by Prime Minister Rishi Sunak and English Heritage curators appeal to tradition by emphasizing the historical significance and treasured status of Stonehenge as a UNESCO World Heritage Site to condemn the protesters' actions.
The commenter's statement criticizing the protest as vandalism and not effective appeals to the traditional view of respecting historical monuments and conventional methods of activism.

Rajan Naidu draws a questionable conclusion by comparing the need for a Fossil Fuel Non-Proliferation Treaty to past international actions on nuclear weapons without considering the differences in complexity and impact of the issues.

cases.name: Jimmy Kimmel Exposes Fox News Plan to Spin a Biden Debate Victory

sentences.1: Late-night host Jimmy Kimmel thinks Fox News is scared of how Donald Trump will perform when he takes to the stage at the first presidential debate of the 2024 election, scheduled for June 27.
sentences.2: "The gang at Fox News is hard at work coming up with an excuse for if Biden does well at the debate," Kimmel said. "After spending the past two nights peddling a very misleading clip that claims to show Biden freezing up, Sean Hannity's now back to the 'if Trump loses the debate, it's because Biden's on drugs' routine."
sentences.3: Kimmel showed a clip of Hannity arguing to Lara Trump this week that Biden will likely be taking some sort of drug during the debate, be it coffee or something slightly more nefarious-mirroring Trump's claim in April that Biden was "higher than a kite" during his 2024 State of the Union address.
sentences.4: Hannity backed the idea that Biden should be drug-tested, and Kimmel was happy to call his bluff: "Let's do it. Let's test the president for caffeine. Let's test Trump for Adderall and Cialis. Let's see how the tests come out."
sentences.5: Kimmel mocked the very idea of Biden relying on any special stimulant drug for his big public appearances. "I mean, who in the world is buying this idea that there's some magic debate pill you can take… It's all nuts. It's just all nuttiness."
sentences.6: The late-night host also marveled at how Biden got Trump to agree to the debate rules, which include muting candidates when it's not their time to talk and not allowing either candidate to bring notes on stage with them.
sentences.7: "Trump has apparently agreed to these rules," Kimmel said, "which is something to keep in mind ten days from now when he claims the whole thing was rigged against him."

Explanation.explanation: The late-night host is implying that because Trump agreed to the debate rules, it should be considered a tradition or precedent that he will later claim the debate was rigged against him. This is an appeal to tradition as it tries to justify a future action based on a past agreement.

The conclusion that Trump will claim the whole debate was rigged against him based on his agreement to the rules is questionable as it assumes a future event based on a current decision without strong evidence.

The discussion of Trump agreeing to debate rules and the potential claim of rigging serves as a distraction from the main topic of Fox News potentially spinning a Biden debate victory. It diverts attention from the primary issue at hand.

cases.name: Biden's D-Day Speech Nailed the Threat of Modern Fascism

sentences.1: Speaking on sacred ground in Normandy, the president correctly drew parallels between America's enemies in World War II and the threats we face domestically and globally today.
sentences.2: Watching the small parade of elderly men and womenâ€”many in wheelchairs, some wearing military insigniaâ€”receive the gratitude of the President of the United States and the leaders of the Western world on the 80th anniversary of D-Day was profoundly moving. sentences.3: You saved the world,' said Joe Biden to one of the veterans of the battle. And we know there was no hyperbole in the comment. sentences.4: Infused in the remarks however, there was a sense that while the D-Day landings marked a turning point and the beginning of the end of World War II, even that great victory had not put an end to the kind of threats the world faced from the Nazis and fascists of the middle of the last century.
sentences.5: You could hear it in the words of President Biden when he said, 'To surrender to bullies, to bow down to dictators is simply unthinkable! Were we to do that, it means we'd be forgetting what happened here on these hallowed beaches.'
sentences.6: Surveying the last few surviving heroes of that long-ago war, he made it clear that we had an obligation to themâ€”and to those who had fallen beside themâ€”to continue to fight threats against democracy, against our values, against our allies as they had once done.
sentences.7: He was specific about the nature of one of those threats, another war raging in Europe as the result of the aggression of a ruthless dictator. He said that to be 'worthy' of the sacrifices made on D-Day and throughout the Second World War, we must now fight against tyranny once again, this time in Ukraine.
sentences.8: 'The fact that they were heroes,' he reminded the audience of world leaders and those watching worldwide, 'does not absolve us of what we have to do today.'
sentences.9: Biden's remarks were pointed and powerfully delivered. He underscored that NATO, the successor to the Allies that achieved victory in the most costly war the world has ever known, was 'more united than ever.'
sentences.10: 'Make no mistake,' he intoned, 'we will never bow down.'
sentences.11: But his message was not intended solely for our one World War II ally that has over the decades since become one of our principal adversaries: Russia. There were in his words messages for political adversaries at home who did not seem to understand why we fought in World War II.
sentences.12: Some of those were the members of the GOP MAGA alliance that for months blocked aid to Ukraine and who have madeâ€”much like those who opposed U.S. involvement in the Second World Warâ€”'America First' their rallying cry. To them, Biden said, 'Isolation was not the answer 80 years ago and is not the answer today.'
sentences.13: But in his remarks, he also subtly but unmistakably evoked perhaps the darkest of the specters haunting Thursday's ceremonies, the U.S. and our modern alliance. 'We know the dark forces that these heroes fought against 80 years ago; they never fade. Aggression and greed, the desire to dominate and controlâ€¦ these are perennial. The struggle between dictatorship and freedom is unending.'
sentences.14: With these words, Biden addressed the bitter irony that haunted the commemoration ceremonies. While D-Day occurred eight decades ago, America is now just five months from an election that could bring to power a man and a movement who embody and celebrate the twisted authoritarian values of the enemies we sought to defeat so long ago.
sentences.15: Fascism has not gone away. The tactics of the Nazis to employ racism and demagoguery to divide society and enable their seizure of power and their gutting of democratic institutions currently are the playbook of Donald Trump and the MAGA movement.
sentences.16: Biden's respect and profound appreciation for those who died fighting Hitler and Mussolini stood in stark contrast to the remarks of Trump, six years ago, on a similarly intended visit, when he reportedly called the fallen heroes 'suckers' and 'losers.'
sentences.17: But the day and night differences between the two leaders, as we now know, go much further.

Trump's core campaign tactic in the wake of his defeat in 2020 was 'the big lie.' The origin of that approach can be traced directly to Hitler's propaganda minister Joseph Goebbels.
sentences.19: He even recently boosted a video containing subtle support for 'a unified Reich.'
sentences.20: Trump has said he would be a dictator on 'day one.' He has fully embraced fascism. His embrace of fascist techniques and ideas has even been cited by leading experts on fascism.
sentences.21: Biden did not mention Trump by name. But he did not have to. Everyone present understood that the threat the allies sought to defeat in World War II was resurgent in domestic American politics. Indeed, they knew full well of the ties between Biden's 2024 opponent and the tyrant Biden did cite as threatening Ukraine, Vladimir Putin.
sentences.22: They knew that, once again, the world faces a threat from a global right-wing ethno-nationalist alliance that has contempt for democracy and wants to dismantle the international order the U.S. and our allies erected in the wake of the last world war.
sentences.23: It was clear listening to Biden and the other leaders' speeches that Donald Trump, like Vladimir Putin, is not on the side of those heroes we were celebrating.
sentences.24: Trump and the MAGA movement are on the wrong side. They are, in terms that World War II leaders would understand, the enemy. They are no different in many key ways from those who 80 years ago sought to obliterate our institutions and destroy our democracy.
sentences.25: The difference, made clearer than ever with Thursday's ceremonies, is that stark. It is that threatening. Given the nature of the sacrifices made by the Greatest Generation, it is that extraordinary and chilling.
sentences.26: And the implicit message for those who understand where we are today is that our generation faces a test just like those faced by our parents and grandparents in the 1930s and 1940s. sentences.27: Unlike prior generations, however, we are fortunate. Thanks to them, at least right now, at least in the United States, we do not have to lay down our lives to defeat fascism. All we have to do is take the threat seriously and do our duty as citizens by voting.
sentences.28: There could be no greater dishonor done to those who died on D-Day and around the world in World War II than to allow authoritarianism and fascism to triumph in November after so many had sacrificed so much so many years ago to defeat them.

Explanation.explanation: The speaker implies that because threats faced from Nazis and fascists in the past still exist today, we must continue to fight against them as in the past.
By referencing the lessons from World War II and the need to fight against threats today, the speaker appeals to the tradition of overcoming historical challenges.
The speaker draws a conclusion that an election could bring to power a man and a movement embodying authoritarian values without providing sufficient evidence or logical reasoning.
The speaker makes unsupported claims about Trump's actions and statements, linking them to fascism without strong evidence.
The speaker assumes the audience understands the unmentioned connection between Trump and the threats faced in World War II without explicit explanation or justification.
The speaker compares Trump and the MAGA movement to the enemies of World War II without a thorough analysis or clear evidence of similarity.
The speaker presents allowing authoritarianism and fascism to triumph in the election as the greatest dishonor without fully supporting this claim.

cases.name: Biden Brutally Goes After Trump During State of the Unionâ€”Just Not by Name

sentences.1: Biden didn't shy away from attacking Trump or Republicans. But he did shy away from saying Trump's name.
sentences.2: In what could be his final State of the Union address, President Joe Biden poked and prodded Republicans on a number of issuesâ€”Ukraine, abortion, the border, even Jan. 6â€”contrasting GOP apathy with Democratic action as the general election campaign began in earnest Thursday night.
sentences.3: It was an unapologetically political speech, with Biden punching Republicans and Republicans punching right back. But Biden saved his sharpest contrasts, his most direct swipes, for the one Republican whose name he refused to mention: Donald Trump.
sentences.4: Biden repeatedly referenced Trump with titles like 'my predecessor' and 'the former Republican President,' avoiding his name throughout the entire speech even as he called Trump out repeatedly.
sentences.5: Just a few minutes into his address Thursday night, Biden noted that Trump had told Russian President Vladimir Putin to 'do whatever the hell you want' with respect to Ukraine.
sentences.6: "A former American president actually said that, bowing down to a Russian leader," Biden said. "It's outrageous. It's dangerous. It's unacceptable."
sentences.7: But Biden was just getting started with his criticism of Trump.
sentences.8: He dinged 'my predecessor'â€”as well as 'some of you here'â€”for seeking to 'bury the truth' about Jan. 6. 'I will not do that,' Biden said. 'This is a moment to speak the truth and bury the lies.'
sentences.9: He attacked 'my predecessor' for trying to overturn Roe v. Wade. 'He's the reason it was overturned. In fact, he brags about it,' Biden said.
sentences.10: He called out 'my predecessor' for his record on COVID and causing a 'mental health crisis of isolation and loneliness.' Biden said Trump 'failed the most basic duty'â€”'the duty to care.'
sentences.11: He went on to accuse 'my predecessor' of not buying American, of trying to take away health insurance for Americans, and of demanding that Republicans block a bipartisan border bill.
sentences.12: Biden's constant calls back to 'my predecessor' served multiple purposes. He was able to get overtly political without directlyâ€”by nameâ€”attacking Trump. But Biden also subtly connected the former president to the past, not the future, as both men argue about their age, ability, and record.
sentences.13: It was the topic of immigration, however, where Biden delivered his most relentless attacks on Trump and Republicans. He accused the GOP of 'playing politics' with border security so they could preserve immigration as a campaign issue for Trump.
sentences.14: "I'm told my predecessor called Republicans in Congress and demanded they block the bill," Biden said. "He feels it would be a political win for me and a political loser for him."
sentences.15: At another point, Biden contrasted himself with 'my predecessor' for offering a comprehensive immigration plan and making good on a bipartisan proposal to 'secure the border.'
sentences.16: Ever since Republicans followed Trump's orders to reject the bipartisan border security deal, Democrats have taken a more aggressive immigration posture on the campaign trail. sentences.17: Biden was so aggressive on immigration that he even went toe-to-toe with one of the most predictable troublemakers in Congress: Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene (R-GA). In a testy, unscripted exchange, Biden responded to Greeneâ€”who was violating House rules by wearing a MAGA hat on the House floorâ€”as she demanded Biden acknowledge Laken Riley, a 22-year-old nursing student who police say was murdered by an undocumented immigrant.
sentences.18: Biden called Riley 'an innocent young woman who was killed.' And Biden adoptedâ€”either intentionally or notâ€”GOP rhetoric on immigrants as he referred to Riley's killer as 'an illegal.'
sentences.19: While he certainly didn't score any points with progressives for that dehumanizing term, he did seem to neutralize a Republican talking point about his refusal to address the murder.
sentences.20: Overall, however, this was a speech for Democrats. Biden used the State of the Union as an opportunity to run through Democratic accomplishments during the first years of his presidency, like an infrastructure bill, an economy that has defied expectations, and a prescription drug bill that lowered the cost of insulin to $35 a month for seniors.
sentences.21: Biden also noted that Democrats passed the bipartisan Safer Communities Actâ€”the first major gun safety bill in three decades. (Meanwhile, Biden said, his 'predecessor' told the NRA that he was 'proud he did nothing on guns when he was president.' After a school shooting in Iowa, Biden also accurately recounted that Trump told people to 'get over it.')
sentences.22: Biden additionally tried to move the needle on stubborn negative perceptions of the economy by championing economic indicators that are trending in a positive direction after the COVID-19 pandemic.
sentences.23: "I inherited an economy that was on the brink," he said. "Now our economy is the envy of the world."
sentences.24: Biden made a conscious effort to brag about the economy, a departure from previous joint addresses when Biden was tentative about his economic accomplishments. This time, he boasted about 15 million new jobs in three years, unemployment near 50-year lows, and steady wage growth.
sentences.25: But Biden also didn't shirk away from addressing inflation. He instead tried to empathize with Americans who still face the challenges of rising costs and presented it as a problem that Republicans were refusing to address.
sentences.26: "Snack companies think you won't notice when they charge you just as much for the same size bag but with fewer chips in it," Biden said with a laugh, imploring lawmakers to pass Sen. Bob Casey's (D-PA) bill to 'put a stop to shrinkflation.'
sentences.27: Biden seemed determined to make headlines for the political nature of his one hour and seven minute speech rather than giving a 'sleepy' address. sentences.28: The strategy seemed to work. Republicans emerged from the House chamber offended and ready to criticize Biden for his partisan shots, but what they weren't doing was making the same jokes about his old age and confusion that kicked off the night.
